title: Low Molecular Weight Protein Enrichment on Mesoporous Silica Thin Films for Biomarker Discovery
protocol: Create the coating solution for the chip by mixing 14 mL of tetraethylorthosilicate (TEOS) with 17 mL of ethanol, 6.5 mL of deionized water and 0.5 mL of 6M HCl under strong stirring.
Heat this mixture at 80 °C for 2 hours while maintaining constant stirring.
Prepare polymer solutions by adding the desired tri-block copolymer to 10 mL of ethanol with strong stirring.
Mix 7.5 ml of the silicate solution into the tri-block copolymer solution and stir strongly for 2 hours at room temperature.
Apply 1 mL of coating solution to a 4 inch silicon wafer by spin-coating at 1500 rpm for 20 seconds.
Heat the coated wafer at 80 °C for 12 hours.
Remove organic surfactant from films by heating them at 1 °C per minute up to 425 °C, and then baking at this temperature for 5 hours.
Pretreat the mesoporous silica (MPS) chip surface with oxygen plasma ashing using O2 flow rate: 80 sccm, power: 300 W, time: 10 minutes.
Optionally silanate chips in a solution of 3% organosilane in methanol and DI water (19:1) for 72 hours at room temperature.
Rinse the chemically modified chips sequentially with methanol and deionized water.
Cure the treated chips at 110 °C for 15 minutes.
Add TFA and ACN to each serum sample for final concentrations of 0.01% TFA and 5% ACN.
Vortex to mix the samples thoroughly.
Shake the mixed samples on a table vortex shaker at room temperature for 30 minutes.
Pre-bake chips overnight in an oven at 160 °C.
Alternatively, store the chips in a desiccator until ready to use to prevent hydration of the surface by ambient water in air.
Use compressed air to dust off any particles on the chip's surface.
Cut prefabricated, purchased CultureWell chambered coverglass to include the desired number of wells.
Clean coverglass with 100% ethanol and place it on an MPS chip surface.
Press coverglass down with forceps to ensure a complete seal with the chip.
Pipette 10 μL of serum sample into each 3 mm well.
Incubate for 30 minutes in a humidified chamber at room temperature.
Pipette up serum from wells and discard.
Pipette 10 μL of deionized water to each well to wash away larger proteins.
Repeat washing with deionized water four times.
Pipette 5 μL elution buffer (0.1% TFA + 50% ACN) to each sample well.
Mix the elution buffer in each well by pipetting up and down 30 times while moving the pipette tip around in the well.
Apply elution buffer to only one or two samples at a time to prevent evaporation.
Pipette all the elution buffer from each well into a microcentrifuge tube until ready for MALDI-TOF analysis.
Spot 0.5 μL of sample to MALDI target plate and allow to dry.

Spot 0.5 μL matrix (α-cyano-4-hydroxycinnamic acid (CHCA), 5 g/L) or saturated solution of trans-3,5-dimethoxy-4-hydroxycinnamic acid (SA) in 50% acetonitrile containing 0.1% TFA and allow to co-crystallization.
Spot 0.5 μL of calibration solution to each calibration spot and allow to dry.
Insert target plate into MALDI-TOF mass spectrometer.
Set machine to positive reflector mode with a laser intensity of 4200 and 3000 shots per sample.
Select mass range from 800 to 5000 Da with a target mass of 2000 Da.
Perform same MALDI-TOF analysis in linear mode but change the mass range to 900 to 10,000 Da or 3000 to 70,000 Da and a target mass of 5000 Da.
Process raw spectra with ConvertPeakList software.
Export data to SpecAlign software for preprocessing.
Align all spectra using the PAFFT correlation method.
Normalize intensities to total ion current (TIC) in each spectrum.
Smooth spectra with a factor of 4.
De-noise spectra with a factor of 0.5.
Detect peaks with a baseline of 0.5, mass window of 21, and height ratio of 1.5.
Remove negative values before analysis.
Perform hierarchical clustering using Cluster 3.0 software.
Visualize results with MapleTree software.
Log-transform MALDI MS data (m/z peak intensities).
Normalize and median center the log-transformed data.
Calculate distance between samples using Pearson correlation.
Perform complete linkage clustering.
Conduct an independent Student t-test for comparison between groups (n = 2) for each detected MS peak.
Consider a P-value of 0.02 or lower significant to select differentially harvested peptides and proteins among the different mesoporous proteomic chips.
